question: Does Codex 0.160.0's local Responses request place system/developer items in an order or shape that the Qwen chat template cannot accept, and can a tiny stateless adapter normalize it without changing the request's meaning?
method: Run one Codex exec request inside a network-isolated bubblewrap namespace against a local fake Responses endpoint. The endpoint records only structural metadata (top-level keys, input item type/role/key list, tool type/name/namespace, instruction length/hash) and returns a deliberate HTTP 500. It does not store prompt or user content.
expected_result: A sanitized structural receipt sufficient to determine whether an adapter can reorder/normalize messages. A captured request is diagnostic evidence only and not a model/tool-loop pass.
abort_conditions: If the CLI attempts a non-loopback request, the network namespace blocks it; stop after the first captured local request.
Do not save full request body, credentials, or full prompt text.
No model or GPU test in this diagnostic.
